newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Burns Philp sees improved results.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Burns Philp sees improved results.

text.p: Food ingredients group Burns Philp and Co Ltd said on Monday it was confident of an improved results performance in the 1996/97 financial year.

"We are confident that based on the first quarter results and trading since then, Burns Philp will continue to improve its performance over the year," Burns Philp managing director Ian Clack told the annual meeting.
Clack said last year's results were not satisfactory and did not reflect the earnings potential of the company's assets.
"Let's make it clear that once we saw adverse trends affecting the results we took immediate corrective action," he said.

"We changed the way we manage the business and we brought in new and experienced executives to drive the company forward," he said. He said changes six months ago to the management of the company from a regional to a customer-based structure and the introduction of new managers were already benefiting customers.
Clack said that over the past financial year, Burns Philp's underlying business grew by nine percent after the effect of foreign exchange and disposed businesses.
But he said slotting fees in the United States, sharp rises in the costs of raw materials and the costs of developing the businesses in Asia had all adversely affected results.
Slotting fees are paid by manufacturers to retailers to ensure their products are placed in an attractive slot on supermarket shelves.
Molasses prices rose 50 percent in the second half of 1995/96 because of higher world grain prices.
Molasses is the main raw material used to produce yeast.
"We have since seen an encouraging downward trend in some key raw material costs in this financial year," Clack said.

Acting chairman William Irvine said that while Burns Philp had not paid a final dividend in 1995/96, the company's usual policy remains that a dividend of 65 to 75 percent of operating profit after tax and before abnormals should be paid.
Burns Philp posted a 28 percent fall in trading profit before abnornals of A$74.8 million in the 1995/96 year.
